text:
maria: Quick heads-up — profiler on prod3 shows unexpected allocator churn when AWQ + FP8 + dynamic batching (batch_size ramp to 16). Repro after kernel routing fallback triggered. Flamegraph and heap samples attached in the run.

lee: link?

maria: https://perf.srv/runs/1872/flamegraph.png
Also the short log paste:
```
alloc_events: 124,102
free_events: 123,845
peak_device_rss: 13.2GB
worker_hwm: 12.7GB
observed_fragmentation: 18%
hotstack: kv_cache_promote -> slab_alloc -> kernel_select
```

oren: hmm. The pattern looks like lots of small frees between large alloc spikes. Sounds like workspace slicing + deferred_free window racing with kernel fallback. We saw similar with AWQ dtype upcasts a month ago.

sasha: @maria can you confirm whether the KV cache dtype promotion path is enabled (auto-promote to fp16 for kv) in that canary? If promotion runs mid-request it can blow up transient working set.

maria: confirmed — auto-promote enabled in this canary (we turned it on to reduce token size). Repro steps in the run: use model awq-mix-7b, input lengths ~1200, batching hint dynamic, fallback policy "latency-first -> cost-fallback".

devon: If auto-promote is the culprit, two low-friction mitigations: 1) bump per-worker workspace_slice from 64MB -> 128MB; 2) extend deferred_free window by +50ms so compaction can happen before next allocation. Both are config flags and safe to A/B.

maria: I tried a quick local tweak: workspace_slice=128MB + deferred_free=120ms. One-shot run shows allocations stabilized and frees coalesced. p50 down ~7%, p99 down ~10%.

perf-bot: ALERT: perf-regression detected on canary 1872. commit abc123 -> p99 latency +18% vs baseline (24h). Observed correlating spike in device allocation churn.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-02T08:12 triggered rollback-policy? no, it's still active. Tag: canary/awq-auto-promote

lee: We should avoid long-term workspace increase because that increases memory pressure for other models. Can we instead gate auto-promote: only promote on cold-start, not mid-request? Or do a lazy prefix-only upcast for KV to avoid full-array transient growth.

oren: Good idea. Also consider compact-reclaim on idle (touch compaction) that runs when worker utilization < 10% for 100ms. That reduces fragmentation without permanent larger slices.

sasha: I'll spin up two quick canaries tonight: A) workspace_slice=128MB + deferred_free=120ms B) gate-auto-promote-to-cold-start + lazy-kv-upcast. Compare p99 and memory HWM.

maria: Thanks. I opened a short ticket: https://redwood/issues/INF-4823 with repro, logs, and the flamegraph. Assigning to @sasha for canaries and @oren for allocator idea follow-up.

devon: I'll add a quick fallback patch: if allocator_frag > 15% and batch_size > 8 then prefer kernel_variant that favors compact memory path (slower kernel but lower transient alloc). Low-risk toggle.

lee: Great. Keep notes in the ticket about cost impact — bigger workspaces => more reserved memory per worker => fewer concurrent slots.

maria: Final: immediate next steps — sasha run canaries (A/B), oren prototype compact-reclaim hook, devon prepare kernel_variant toggle. We'll meet 30m after canary finishes and decide rollback or promote. :thumbsup:
